zh.summary: Cyber Kill Chain 看階段，MITRE ATT&CK 看目的與行為；分類不是成功證明，結論要跟著證據走。

sourceBody.text: CEH M01-05｜Cyber Kill Chain 與 MITRE ATT&CK
網路攻擊鏈與攻擊者行為分析：從「被駭客攻擊」到「看懂整個攻擊過程」
Module 01：Introduction to Ethical Hacking（道德駭客入門）
編輯補充：銀行與Northstar都是合成教材情境，只討論辨識與防禦，不操作第三方目標。
建議學習時間：12～15 分鐘｜難度：初學者 ★★☆☆☆
一、先掌握結論：為什麼我們需要這兩套框架？
假設你是某家公司的資訊安全工程師。
今天早上，老闆突然跑來告訴你：
「我們公司好像被駭客入侵了！你趕快查一下！」
這時候，你會遇到幾個問題：
1. 駭客到底是怎麼進來的？
2. 他已經做到哪個程度了？
3. 他可能使用了哪些攻擊方法？
4. 我們有沒有辦法阻止他？
5. 哪些事情已經證實，哪些只是懷疑？
這正是今天要學習的兩套框架所要解決的問題。

rows: 攻擊者戰術與技術知識庫
攻擊者做了什麼、目的是什麼？
理解攻擊過程、尋找阻斷時機
分析攻擊行為、設計偵測方法
戰術、技術、子技術與具體做法

sourceBody.text: 最重要的一句話：
Cyber Kill Chain 告訴你「整起攻擊的發展過程」；MITRE ATT&CK 告訴你「攻擊者使用了哪些方法」。
MITRE 官方也明確指出，兩套框架是互補的；Cyber Kill Chain 偏向高階的攻擊階段，而 ATT&CK 提供更細緻的行為描述。[MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/faq/)
二、Cyber Kill Chain：把駭客攻擊想像成一場銀行搶案
2.1 什麼是 Cyber Kill Chain？
Cyber Kill Chain 是由美國國防與航太公司 Lockheed Martin 提出的攻擊分析模型。
它把典型的網路攻擊分成七個階段。
為什麼要這樣做？
因為駭客通常不是突然就拿到所有資料。
在許多攻擊事件中，攻擊者必須進行資訊蒐集、準備工具、取得進入系統的機會，最後才有可能達成目的。
防守方如果能在中途發現並阻止攻擊，就有機會避免更嚴重的損害。
2.2 七個攻擊階段
我們用銀行搶案來理解。

rows: 與外部同夥聯繫、接收指令

sourceBody.text: 這七個階段是原始 Cyber Kill Chain 模型的核心架構。[www.trendmicro.com](https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/what-is/cyber-attack/cyber-kill-chain.html)

原始來源補充：七階段另對照[Lockheed Martin原始白皮書](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/content/dam/lockheed-martin/rms/documents/cyber/LM-White-Paper-Intel-Driven-Defense.pdf)。本次直接擷取原站回傳403，已核對官方搜尋索引中的七階段原文；不宣稱已完整讀取該PDF。
但要注意，銀行搶案只是幫助理解的比喻，並不代表真實駭客攻擊一定按照這七個階段發生。
接下來，我們換成電腦攻擊的例子。
2.3 實際案例：駭客想要偷走公司的學生資料
假設有一家虛構公司 Northstar，經營線上教學平台。
公司的員工每天使用電子郵件與供應商聯絡。
某天，駭客決定攻擊這家公司。
第一階段：Reconnaissance（偵察）
駭客先從網路上蒐集資訊。
例如，他可能發現公司官網公開了採購部門的電子郵件。
這就是偵察。
但我們不能因為收到釣魚郵件，就直接認定駭客一定事先搜尋過網站。
第二階段：Weaponization（武器化）
駭客準備一個含有惡意內容的附件，並將它包裝成正常的採購文件。
這個階段的重點是「準備攻擊內容」。
通常，這些準備活動發生在攻擊者自己的環境，防守方未必能直接觀察。
第三階段：Delivery（投遞）
駭客將附件寄給公司員工。
這就是投遞。
請特別注意：
寄送郵件成功，不代表攻擊者已經入侵電腦。
就像有人把可疑包裹送到公司，並不代表有人打開包裹。
第四階段：Exploitation（利用）
假設員工開啟附件，而附件成功利用閱讀軟體的安全弱點，讓惡意程式碼執行。
這時候才有證據支持利用弱點的行為已經發生。
不過，開啟附件不一定會造成弱點利用。
有些惡意附件可能透過誘導使用者直接執行程式達成目的，並不涉及軟體漏洞。
第五階段：Installation（安裝）
假設惡意程式接著在電腦上安裝其他惡意元件。
這個動作屬於 Installation。
但有一個重要區別：
- 程式已經執行，不代表已經安裝。
- 程式已經安裝，不代表重新開機後仍可運作。
後者還需要檢查 Persistence（持續存取）相關機制。
第六階段：Command and Control（命令與控制）
這個名稱常縮寫成 C2。
想像駭客雖然已經把惡意程式放進電腦，但他還想從外部操作它。
於是，惡意程式與外部伺服器建立通訊，接收指令並傳送執行結果。
這就是 C2 的典型概念。
但要注意：
電腦連上某個 HTTPS 網站，並不代表正在進行 C2。
正常瀏覽網站、使用雲端服務，也都可能使用 HTTPS。
我們必須結合程序行為、連線目的地及其他證據判斷。
第七階段：Actions on Objectives（執行目標行動）
假設駭客的目標是竊取學生個人資料。
惡意程式可能嘗試讀取相關資料。
但如果系統的權限控制拒絕了這項操作，我們就只能說：
「觀察到未授權的資料存取嘗試，且這次存取遭到拒絕。」
不能說：
「駭客已經成功偷走資料。」
2.4 為什麼這七個階段重要？
因為公司不需要等到資料被偷走，才開始防禦。
例如：
- 郵件安全系統可以在 Delivery 階段阻止惡意附件。
- 修補程式與執行防護可以降低 Exploitation 階段的風險。
- 終端防護可以偵測可疑程式的安裝。
- 網路監控可以發現可疑的 C2 活動。
- 最小權限可以限制攻擊者能夠存取的資料。
這就是 Defense in Depth（縱深防禦） 的概念。
我們不把全部希望寄託在單一防線上。
此外，真實攻擊不一定完整出現七個階段。
例如攻擊者直接使用偷來的合法雲端帳號登入服務，可能不需要先安裝任何惡意程式。
因此，Cyber Kill Chain 是協助分析的模型，不是每起事件都必須填滿的表格。
三、MITRE ATT&CK：駭客到底用了什麼攻擊方法？
理解 Cyber Kill Chain 之後，我們已經知道如何觀察整體攻擊進展。
但還有另一個問題：
同樣是取得系統的初始存取權，駭客可以使用很多不同的方法。
例如：
- 寄送惡意電子郵件。
- 利用對外服務的漏洞。
- 使用已遭竊取的合法帳號。
這些行為的目的可能相同，但使用的方法不同。
MITRE ATT&CK 就是幫我們整理這些行為。
3.1 MITRE ATT&CK 是什麼？
MITRE ATT&CK 是由 MITRE 維護的攻擊者行為知識庫。
它根據實際觀察到的攻擊行為，整理出各種攻擊戰術與技術。
ATT&CK 的主要用途包括：
1. 分析資安事件。
2. 整理網路威脅情報。
3. 設計偵測規則。
4. 評估組織的防禦能力。
ATT&CK 目前也區分 Enterprise、Mobile 與 ICS 等領域，分別涵蓋企業資訊環境、行動裝置與工業控制系統。[MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/)
你可以把它理解成一本：
「駭客攻擊行為百科全書」。
但它並不是攻擊工具，也不是所有駭客行為的完整清單。
3.2 先學會四個最重要的名詞
這四個名詞是本堂課的核心。
我們用「駭客寄送惡意附件」理解。
第一層：Tactic（戰術）
戰術指的是攻擊者的目的。
例如：
Initial Access（初始存取）
駭客想取得進入目標系統的機會。
這是他的目的。
第二層：Technique（技術）
技術指的是攻擊者打算用什麼方法。
例如：
Phishing（釣魚攻擊）
駭客可能藉由假冒可信任的人或組織，誘導受害者採取某些行動。
在 MITRE ATT&CK 中，這項技術的編號是：
第三層：Sub-technique（子技術）
釣魚攻擊有不同類型。
例如：
- 用電子郵件附件。
- 用電子郵件連結。
- 透過第三方服務傳送釣魚訊息。
其中，使用針對性的惡意附件進行釣魚，稱為：
Spearphishing Attachment（魚叉式釣魚附件）
編號是：
這個編號是真實存在的 ATT&CK 子技術，歸類於 Initial Access 戰術。[MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/)
來源校訂：附件原連結使用舊頁T1193；這裡改連現行T1566.001官方頁。原文快照保留舊連結，概念編號並未改變。
第四層：Procedure（具體做法）
現在假設駭客寄送一封電子郵件：
寄件者假冒公司的供應商。
郵件標題是：
「10 月份採購明細，請確認。」
附件裡面包含惡意程式。
這就是這次假想事件中的具體做法。
請注意，Procedure 不一定有自己的 T 編號。
它描述的是特定事件中，攻擊者實際如何運用某項技術。
3.3 把四個層次串起來
現在，你已經可以理解以下架構：

Tactic（戰術）
│
└── Initial Access
    想取得初始存取機會
    │
    └── Technique（技術）
        │
        └── Phishing（T1566）
            使用釣魚攻擊
            │
            └── Sub-technique（子技術）
                │
                └── Spearphishing Attachment
                    T1566.001
                    使用針對性的惡意附件
                    │
                    └── Procedure（具體做法）
                        假冒供應商寄送
                        惡意採購明細附件
這就是 MITRE ATT&CK 的基本邏輯。
你以後看到任何 ATT&CK 技術，都可以問：
「這項技術想達到什麼目的？實際採用了什麼方法？」
四、兩套框架如何一起使用？
這是本堂課最重要的整合觀念。
假設調查人員已經取得充分證據，確認 Northstar 發生以下事件：

惡意元件透過 HTTPS 接收外部指令

sourceBody.text: 你可以發現：
Cyber Kill Chain 讓我們了解事件發展到了哪個階段。
ATT&CK 則讓我們進一步描述具體的攻擊技術。
這裡出現另外兩個重要的 ATT&CK 編號。
T1203：Exploitation for Client Execution
意思是攻擊者利用使用者端軟體的漏洞來執行程式碼。
例如利用有安全弱點的文件閱讀軟體。
但如果只是使用者自行執行惡意程式，就不能在沒有漏洞利用證據的情況下，直接套用 T1203。[MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/)
T1071.001：Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
意思是攻擊者利用 HTTP、HTTPS 等網頁通訊協定進行 C2。
但正常 HTTPS 流量不等於 C2。
必須有其他證據支持該通訊確實被用於攻擊者的命令與控制。[MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/)
一個特別容易搞混的地方
ATT&CK 裡面有 Initial Access、Execution、Persistence、Discovery、Collection、Exfiltration 等戰術。
這些戰術並不是要求攻擊者按照固定順序完成的關卡。
例如：
攻擊者可能已經有合法的雲端帳號，直接使用它存取資料。
此時未必出現惡意程式安裝的階段。
Cyber Kill Chain 是高階階段模型；ATT&CK 是行為分類模型。不要強迫兩套框架逐項對應。
五、資安分析真正困難的地方：如何判斷證據？
現在，我們進一步思考。
假設你是負責調查事件的資訊安全工程師。
你發現公司收到一封釣魚郵件。
這樣就能說公司被駭客入侵了嗎？
不能。
因為我們必須區分：
觀察到某個行為，不代表該行為已經達成攻擊者的目的。
我們來看五種可能的情況。

rows: 發現惡意郵件遭閘道隔離
發現並阻擋一次可疑郵件活動
攻擊者已取得最高權限
確認惡意程式與外部 C2 通訊
紀錄顯示未授權讀取遭拒絕
這次未授權存取被阻擋

sourceBody.text: 這裡有一個非常重要的觀念：
沒有找到證據，不等於證明事情沒有發生
例如：
你檢查公司電腦的紀錄，沒有找到惡意附件執行的事件。
可能有兩種解釋。
第一種：附件確實沒有執行。
第二種：附件曾經執行，但相關紀錄不存在、沒有被蒐集，或已超過保存期限。
因此，專業的分析員應該說：
「目前沒有發現附件執行的證據。」
而不是直接宣稱：
「我們已經證明附件絕對沒有執行。」
這兩句話的證據強度不同。
六、從攻擊框架走向實際防禦
理解攻擊者的行為後，下一步不是急著學習更多攻擊工具。
而是思考：
我們應該在哪個環節阻止攻擊，又該蒐集什麼證據證明防護有效？
沿用剛才的 Northstar 案例。
防線一：電子郵件安全
目標是降低惡意附件到達使用者的機會。
可能使用：
- 郵件過濾。
- 惡意附件掃描。
- 郵件隔離。
驗證時要看：
郵件真的被阻擋了，還是系統只有發出警告？
防線二：終端安全
假設惡意附件仍然被開啟。
這時候，我們希望電腦上的防護措施可以降低惡意程式碼執行的機會。
可能使用：
- 安全性更新。
- 應用程式執行控制。
- EDR（Endpoint Detection and Response，端點偵測與回應）。
驗證時要看：
系統是否實際阻止不當執行，還是僅記錄了事件？
防線三：資料存取控制
假設前面幾層都沒有完全擋住攻擊。
我們還能透過最小權限原則，降低攻擊者能夠接觸的資料範圍。
例如：
採購部門的電腦原則上不應擁有讀取所有學生私人作答資料的權限。
即使惡意程式在這台電腦上執行，也不代表它能直接存取所有資料。
這就是最小權限（Principle of Least Privilege）的價值。
不過，仍必須考慮權限提升、憑證遭竊等其他風險。
七、銜接前四堂：我們正在建立完整的資安思考架構
把 M01-01 到 M01-05 串起來，你會看到一個完整的分析流程。

rows: 我們要保護什麼安全目標？
什麼可能受損？風險在哪裡？
我們可以合法測試什麼？
哪些地方可能成為攻擊入口？
攻擊怎麼發展？具體用了什麼方法？

sourceBody.text: 例如：
某家公司有一個對外開放的電子郵件服務。
我們可以這樣思考：
第一步：M01-01
公司要保護學生資料的機密性。
第二步：M01-02
學生資料是重要資產，未授權存取可能造成風險。
第三步：M01-03
我們要確認哪些系統可以接受授權測試。
第四步：M01-04
電子郵件是可能接觸員工的管道；釣魚郵件可能成為攻擊向量。
第五步：M01-05
如果真的發生可疑事件，就使用 Cyber Kill Chain 分析攻擊進展，再利用 MITRE ATT&CK 描述具體行為。
整個邏輯可以整理為：

確認安全目標
      ↓
辨識資產與風險
      ↓
確認合法授權範圍
      ↓
分析攻擊面與攻擊向量
      ↓
辨識攻擊階段
      ↓
分析具體攻擊行為
      ↓
檢查證據與防禦措施
      ↓
提出改善建議
這就是資安工程師開始建立系統性判斷能力的方式。
八、CEH 考試：這一課要優先記住什麼？
先掌握四個考點。
考點一：Cyber Kill Chain 的七個階段
至少要知道七個階段的名稱、意思與基本順序。
尤其要區分：
Delivery、Exploitation、Installation、Command and Control。
考點二：MITRE ATT&CK 的分類邏輯
這部分最重要的是：
- Tactic：Why，為什麼？
- Technique：How，怎麼做？
- Sub-technique：更細的行為類型。
- Procedure：特定事件實際採用的做法。
考點三：認識常見技術編號
本堂課先掌握三個：

rows: 針對性的惡意附件釣魚
利用使用者端軟體漏洞執行程式碼
利用網頁協定進行命令與控制

sourceBody.text: 這三個編號有助於你學會查閱 ATT&CK，但不代表 CEH 只會考這三個，也不代表它們是官方公布的必考題。
考點四：兩套框架的差異
如果題目問：
「哪一套模型將典型網路攻擊分成七個階段？」
答案方向是 Cyber Kill Chain。
如果題目問：
「哪一套知識庫可以用來描述攻擊者的戰術、技術與子技術？」
答案方向是 MITRE ATT&CK。
九、課堂理解檢核
現在用一個簡單的案例，確認你是否真正理解，而不只是記住英文名稱。
情境題
某家公司收到一封假冒供應商的電子郵件。
郵件附件含有惡意程式。
幸好公司的電子郵件安全閘道成功將它隔離。
目前沒有發現附件曾在員工電腦上執行的證據。
但是，一位資安分析員在報告中寫道：
「這封郵件符合 MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001，因此可以確認駭客已經成功入侵公司，並竊取內部資料。」
請回答三個問題：
1. 這個事件比較符合 Cyber Kill Chain 的哪個階段？
2. T1566.001 這個編號代表什麼？它能證明駭客成功入侵嗎？
3. 你認為分析員的結論哪裡有問題？如果由你撰寫報告，你會怎麼修改？
請直接用自己的話回答，不需要背英文名稱。
我會根據你的答案檢查理解程度，並補充需要修正的觀念。
本堂課的最後一句話
Cyber Kill Chain 讓我們理解攻擊如何發展；MITRE ATT&CK 讓我們理解攻擊者如何行動；而證據，才是判斷攻擊是否真的成功的依據。
官方延伸閱讀：[MITRE ATT&CK 入門指南](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/)。

sourceBody.summary: 展開參考解答｜問題一｜比較符合哪個階段？
paragraphs: Delivery（投遞）階段的攻擊嘗試。惡意附件郵件已被郵件閘道隔離，不能把投遞嘗試當成附件已送達員工信箱，更不能推論附件已執行。

sourceBody.summary: 展開參考解答｜問題二｜T1566.001能證明成功入侵嗎？
paragraphs: 它是Spearphishing Attachment，也就是針對性的惡意附件釣魚。這個編號是描述方法的分類標籤，不是成功證明。即使行為符合這個分類，仍須另查開啟、執行、權限及存取紀錄。

sourceBody.summary: 展開參考解答｜問題三｜分析員哪裡推論過頭？
paragraphs: 他把「觀察到釣魚手法」跳成「成功入侵又竊取資料」，中間缺少執行、系統控制與資料外傳證據。
可以改寫：「發現一封假冒供應商、帶有惡意附件的郵件，符合T1566.001行為描述；郵件閘道已將此封郵件隔離。目前未發現該附件在員工端執行或資料遭竊的證據，仍需確認紀錄的涵蓋範圍與完整性。」
不要把「這次隔離成功」擴大成「全公司從未遭攻擊」，也不要把未找到證據說成已證明沒有發生。

sourceBody.text: 解答已公布不等於本人已作答或理解；本次是同一概念的全文修訂，不新增交付次數。

en.summary: Cyber Kill Chain describes stages; MITRE ATT&CK describes objectives and behaviors. Classification is not proof of success.

sourceBody.text: CEH M01-05 | Cyber Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK
Attack chains and adversary behavior analysis: from “we were attacked” to understanding the entire attack process
Module 01: Introduction to Ethical Hacking
Editorial supplement: The bank and Northstar are synthetic teaching scenarios. This lesson discusses identification and defense; no third-party target is tested.
Suggested study time: 12–15 minutes | Difficulty: beginner ★★☆☆☆
1. Start with the conclusion: why do we need these two frameworks?
Suppose you are a company's information security engineer.
This morning, your boss suddenly rushes over and says:
“I think someone has hacked our company! Please investigate immediately!”
You now face several questions:
1. How exactly did the attacker get in?
2. How far have they progressed?
3. Which attack methods might they have used?
4. Can we stop them?
5. What has been established, and what is only suspected?
These are precisely the problems addressed by the two frameworks in today's lesson.

rows: 攻擊者戰術與技術知識庫 (adversary tactics and techniques knowledge base)
Which stage has the attack reached?
What did the attacker do, and what was the objective?
Understand the attack process and identify opportunities for disruption
Analyze attack behaviors and design detection methods

sourceBody.text: The most important sentence:
Cyber Kill Chain describes “how the overall attack develops”; MITRE ATT&CK describes “which methods the attacker uses.”

MITRE also explicitly explains that the frameworks complement each other: Cyber Kill Chain focuses on higher-level attack stages, while ATT&CK provides more detailed descriptions of behavior. [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/faq/)
2. Cyber Kill Chain: imagine a cyberattack as a bank robbery
2.1 What is Cyber Kill Chain?
Cyber Kill Chain is an attack-analysis model introduced by Lockheed Martin, a U.S. defense and aerospace company.
It divides a typical cyberattack into seven stages.
Why do this?
Attackers do not usually obtain all the data out of nowhere.
In many incidents, they must collect information, prepare tools and gain an opportunity to enter the system before they can achieve their objective.
If defenders detect and interrupt an attack along the way, they may prevent more serious damage.
2.2 The seven attack stages
Let us use a bank robbery as an analogy.

rows: Studying the bank's location and security
Bringing the tools to the target location
Placing tools that can be used later
Contacting outside accomplices and receiving instructions

sourceBody.text: These seven stages form the core structure of the original Cyber Kill Chain model. [www.trendmicro.com](https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/what-is/cyber-attack/cyber-kill-chain.html)

Primary-source supplement: The seven stages are also supported by the [original Lockheed Martin white paper](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/content/dam/lockheed-martin/rms/documents/cyber/LM-White-Paper-Intel-Driven-Defense.pdf). Direct retrieval returned 403 during this check; the seven-stage statement was verified in the official-source search index. This does not claim a full PDF review.
Remember that a bank robbery is only a learning analogy. It does not mean real cyberattacks necessarily follow all seven stages.
Next, let us switch to a computer-attack example.
2.3 Worked example: an attacker wants to steal the company's student data
Suppose a fictional company called Northstar operates an online learning platform.
Its employees use email every day to communicate with suppliers.
One day, an attacker decides to target the company.
Stage 1: Reconnaissance
The attacker first gathers information online.
For example, they might discover that the company's website publishes the purchasing department's email address.
This is reconnaissance.
However, receiving a phishing email does not let us conclude that the attacker definitely searched the website beforehand.
Stage 2: Weaponization
The attacker prepares an attachment containing malicious content and disguises it as a normal purchasing document.
The emphasis at this stage is “preparing the attack content.”
These preparations usually occur in the attacker's own environment, so defenders may not be able to observe them directly.
Stage 3: Delivery
The attacker emails the attachment to an employee.
This is delivery.
Pay particular attention to this:
Successfully sending an email does not mean the attacker has compromised a computer.
It is like delivering a suspicious package to a company: delivery does not mean someone opened it.
Stage 4: Exploitation
Suppose the employee opens the attachment, and it successfully exploits a security weakness in the reader software to execute malicious code.
Only then is there evidence supporting the conclusion that exploitation occurred.
However, opening an attachment does not necessarily result in exploitation of a vulnerability.
Some malicious attachments achieve their purpose by persuading the user to execute a program directly, without exploiting a software flaw.
Stage 5: Installation
Suppose the malicious program then installs additional malicious components on the computer.
That action belongs to Installation.
But there is an important distinction:
- A program executing does not mean it has been installed.
- A program being installed does not mean it can still operate after a restart.
The latter requires examination of mechanisms related to persistence.
Stage 6: Command and Control
This is commonly abbreviated as C2.
Imagine that the attacker has placed malware on the computer but also wants to control it from outside.
The malware therefore communicates with an external server, receiving instructions and sending execution results.
This is the typical idea behind C2.
But remember:
A computer connecting to an HTTPS website does not mean C2 is taking place.
Normal web browsing and cloud services can also use HTTPS.
We must assess process behavior, connection destinations and other evidence together.
Stage 7: Actions on Objectives
Suppose the attacker's objective is to steal students' personal information.
The malicious program may attempt to read the relevant data.
If the system's access controls deny that operation, we can say only:
“An unauthorized data-access attempt was observed, and this access was denied.”
We cannot say:
“The attacker successfully stole the data.”
2.4 Why do these seven stages matter?
A company does not have to wait until data is stolen before defending itself.
For example:
- Email security can block malicious attachments during Delivery.
- Patches and execution protection can reduce risk during Exploitation.
- Endpoint protection can detect suspicious program installation.
- Network monitoring can identify suspicious C2 activity.
- Least privilege can limit the data an attacker can access.
This illustrates defense in depth.
We do not place all our hopes in one defensive layer.
Also, real attacks do not necessarily exhibit all seven stages.
For example, an attacker who signs in directly with a stolen, valid cloud account may not need to install any malware first.
Cyber Kill Chain is therefore an aid to analysis, not a form that must be completely filled out for every incident.
3. MITRE ATT&CK: which attack methods did the adversary actually use?
After learning Cyber Kill Chain, we know how to examine the overall progress of an attack.
But another question remains:
Attackers can use many different methods to achieve initial access to a system.
For example:
- Sending malicious email.
- Exploiting a vulnerability in a public-facing service.
- Using a stolen, valid account.
These behaviors may have the same objective but use different methods.
MITRE ATT&CK helps organize these behaviors.
3.1 What is MITRE ATT&CK?
MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of adversary behavior maintained by MITRE.
It organizes attack tactics and techniques based on behavior observed in real attacks.
Major uses of ATT&CK include:
1. Analyzing security incidents.
2. Organizing cyber threat intelligence.
3. Designing detection rules.
4. Assessing an organization's defensive capabilities.

ATT&CK also distinguishes domains such as Enterprise, Mobile and ICS, covering enterprise information environments, mobile devices and industrial control systems respectively. [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/)
You can think of it as:
An encyclopedia of adversary attack behaviors.
But it is not an attack tool or a complete list of every possible adversary behavior.
3.2 First learn the four most important terms
These four terms are central to this lesson.

rows: Which more specific type of method?
How was it actually done in this incident?

sourceBody.text: We will use “an attacker sends a malicious attachment” to understand them.
First level: Tactic
A tactic describes the attacker's objective.
For example:
Initial Access
The attacker wants an opportunity to enter the target system.
That is the objective.
Second level: Technique
A technique describes the method the attacker intends to use.
For example:
Phishing
An attacker might impersonate a trusted person or organization to persuade a victim to take certain actions.
In MITRE ATT&CK, this technique has the identifier:
Third level: Sub-technique
There are different types of phishing.
For example:
- Using email attachments.
- Using email links.
- Sending phishing messages through third-party services.
Phishing with a targeted malicious attachment is called:
Spearphishing Attachment
Its identifier is:
This is a real ATT&CK sub-technique classified under the Initial Access tactic. [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/)

Source correction: The attachment linked to the older T1193 page. The displayed link now points to the current T1566.001 official page. The original snapshot preserves the old link; the concept identifier is unchanged.
Fourth level: Procedure
Now suppose the attacker sends an email:
The sender impersonates the company's supplier.
The subject is:
“October purchasing details—please confirm.”
The attachment contains malware.
This is the procedure in this hypothetical incident.
Notice that a procedure does not necessarily have its own T identifier.
It describes how an attacker actually applies a technique in a particular incident.
3.3 Connect the four levels
You can now understand the following structure:

Tactic
|
+-- Initial Access
    Seeking an initial access opportunity
    |
    +-- Technique
        |
        +-- Phishing (T1566)
            Using a phishing attack
            |
            +-- Sub-technique
                |
                +-- Spearphishing Attachment
                    T1566.001
                    Using a targeted malicious attachment
                    |
                    +-- Procedure
                        Impersonating a supplier to send
                        a malicious purchasing-details attachment
This is the basic logic of MITRE ATT&CK.
Whenever you encounter an ATT&CK technique, ask:
“What objective does this technique serve, and which method was actually used?”
4. How can the two frameworks be used together?
This is the most important integration concept in the lesson.
Suppose investigators have obtained sufficient evidence to confirm the following events at Northstar:

rows: The attacker sends a malicious attachment
The attachment exploits a vulnerability in reader software to execute code
A malicious component receives external commands over HTTPS

sourceBody.text: Notice that:
Cyber Kill Chain helps us understand which stage the incident has reached.
ATT&CK lets us describe the specific attack techniques in greater detail.
Two other important ATT&CK identifiers appear here.
T1203: Exploitation for Client Execution
This means exploiting a vulnerability in client-side software to execute code.
An example is exploiting document-reader software with a security weakness.
If a user simply runs a malicious program, however, we must not automatically apply T1203 without evidence of exploitation. [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/)
T1071.001: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
This means using web communication protocols such as HTTP or HTTPS for C2.
But normal HTTPS traffic does not equal C2.
Other evidence must support that the communication is actually being used for the attacker's command and control. [MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/)
One particularly easy point to confuse
ATT&CK includes tactics such as Initial Access, Execution, Persistence, Discovery, Collection and Exfiltration.
These are not checkpoints that an attacker must complete in a fixed order.
For example:
An attacker may already possess a valid cloud account and use it directly to access data.
A malware-installation stage might not occur at all.
Cyber Kill Chain is a high-level stage model; ATT&CK is a behavior-classification model. Do not force an item-by-item correspondence between them.
5. The real challenge in security analysis: how do we interpret evidence?
Let us think further.
Suppose you are the information security engineer investigating an incident.
You discover that the company received a phishing email.
Can you therefore say that the company was compromised?
No.
We must distinguish this:
Observing a behavior does not mean that the behavior achieved the attacker's objective.
Consider five possible situations.

rows: A malicious email was quarantined by the gateway
A suspicious email activity was detected and blocked
An email reached an employee's inbox
The attacker obtained the highest privileges
Malware communicating with an external C2 was confirmed
Records show that an unauthorized read was denied

sourceBody.text: There is a particularly important point here:
Not finding evidence is not proof that something did not happen
For example:
You examine company computer records and find no event showing execution of the malicious attachment.
There are two possible explanations.
First: the attachment genuinely did not execute.
Second: the attachment executed, but the relevant records do not exist, were not collected or have passed their retention period.
A professional analyst should therefore say:
“No evidence of attachment execution has been found so far.”
Rather than immediately claiming:
“We have proved that the attachment definitely never executed.”
Those statements require different strengths of evidence.
6. From attack frameworks to practical defense
After understanding adversary behavior, the next step is not to rush into learning more attack tools.
Instead, ask:
Where should we stop the attack, and what evidence should we collect to demonstrate that the defenses work?
Continue with the Northstar example.
Defensive layer 1: email security
The objective is to reduce the chance of malicious attachments reaching users.
Possible measures include:
- Email filtering.
- Malicious-attachment scanning.
- Email quarantine.
When verifying effectiveness, ask:
Was the email actually blocked, or did the system merely issue a warning?
Defensive layer 2: endpoint security
Suppose the malicious attachment is opened despite the previous measures.
We then want the computer's protections to reduce the chance of malicious code execution.
Possible measures include:
- Security updates.
- Application execution controls.
- EDR: Endpoint Detection and Response.
When verifying effectiveness, ask:
Did the system actually prevent improper execution, or merely record the event?
Defensive layer 3: data access control
Suppose the earlier layers did not fully block the attack.
Least privilege can still limit the range of data the attacker can reach.
For example:
A purchasing department computer should not ordinarily have permission to read all students' private answer data.
Even if malware runs on that computer, it does not mean the malware can directly access all data.
This is the value of the Principle of Least Privilege.
However, other risks, such as privilege escalation and credential theft, must still be considered.
7. Connecting the first four lessons: building a complete security reasoning framework
Connecting M01-01 through M01-05 reveals a complete analysis process.

rows: Which security objectives are we protecting?
What could be harmed, and where is the risk?
What could become an attack entry point?
How does the attack develop, and which methods are used?
Cyber Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK

sourceBody.text: For example:
A company has an externally accessible email service.
We can reason as follows:
Step 1: M01-01
The company needs to protect the confidentiality of student data.
Step 2: M01-02
Student data is an important asset, and unauthorized access may create risk.
Step 3: M01-03
We must confirm which systems may undergo authorized testing.
Step 4: M01-04
Email is a channel through which employees can be contacted; phishing email may be an attack vector.
Step 5: M01-05
If suspicious activity actually occurs, use Cyber Kill Chain to analyze its progression, then use MITRE ATT&CK to describe the specific behavior.
The overall logic can be organized as:

Confirm security objectives
             ↓
Identify assets and risks
             ↓
Confirm the legally authorized scope
             ↓
Analyze attack surfaces and attack vectors
             ↓
Identify attack stages
             ↓
Analyze specific attack behaviors
             ↓
Examine evidence and defensive measures
             ↓
Recommend improvements
This is how a security engineer begins developing systematic judgment.
8. CEH exam: what should you prioritize in this lesson?
Start with four study points.
Study point 1: the seven Cyber Kill Chain stages
At minimum, know the names, meanings and basic order of the seven stages.
In particular, distinguish:
Delivery, Exploitation, Installation, and Command and Control.
Study point 2: MITRE ATT&CK's classification logic
The important distinctions are:
- Tactic: why?
- Technique: how?
- Sub-technique: a more specific behavior type.
- Procedure: the method actually used in a particular incident.
Study point 3: recognize common technique identifiers
Begin with three in this lesson:

rows: Targeted phishing using a malicious attachment
Exploiting a client-software vulnerability to execute code
Using web protocols for command and control

sourceBody.text: These identifiers help you learn to consult ATT&CK. They do not mean CEH tests only these three, nor that they are officially announced guaranteed exam questions.
Study point 4: differences between the frameworks
If a question asks:
“Which model divides a typical cyberattack into seven stages?”
The answer points to Cyber Kill Chain.
If a question asks:
“Which knowledge base describes adversary tactics, techniques and sub-techniques?”
The answer points to MITRE ATT&CK.
9. Understanding check
Now use a simple example to check whether you genuinely understand, rather than merely remembering the English names.
Scenario
A company receives an email impersonating a supplier.
Its attachment contains malware.
Fortunately, the company's email security gateway successfully quarantines it.
No evidence has currently been found that the attachment executed on an employee computer.
However, a security analyst writes in the report:
“This email matches MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001. We can therefore confirm that the attacker successfully intruded into the company and stole internal data.”
Answer three questions:
1. Which Cyber Kill Chain stage best fits this event?
2. What does T1566.001 represent? Can it prove a successful intrusion?
3. What is wrong with the analyst's conclusion? How would you revise the report?
Answer directly in your own words. You do not need to recite English names.
I will use your answers to check understanding and explain any concepts that need correction.
The final sentence of this lesson
Cyber Kill Chain helps us understand how an attack develops; MITRE ATT&CK helps us understand how the adversary acts; evidence is what determines whether the attack actually succeeded.
Official further reading: [MITRE ATT&CK introductory resources](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/).

sourceBody.summary: Reveal reference answer: Question 1: Which stage fits?
paragraphs: An attempted Delivery. The malicious attachment email was quarantined by the gateway. Do not treat attempted delivery as proof that the message reached an employee mailbox, let alone that its attachment executed.

sourceBody.summary: Reveal reference answer: Question 2: Does T1566.001 prove compromise?
paragraphs: It means Spearphishing Attachment: targeted phishing using a malicious attachment. The identifier classifies a method; it does not certify success. Even when the behavior matches, opening, execution, privileges and access evidence must be checked separately.

sourceBody.summary: Reveal reference answer: Question 3: Where did the analyst overreach?
paragraphs: The analyst jumped from an observed phishing method to successful compromise and theft without evidence of execution, system control or exfiltration.

A better report: “A supplier-impersonation email with a malicious attachment was identified, consistent with T1566.001. The email gateway quarantined this message. No evidence of execution of this attachment on employee endpoints or theft of data has been found so far; logging coverage and completeness still require validation.”
Do not expand successful quarantine of this message into a claim that the whole organization was never attacked. Absence of observed evidence does not prove absence of an event.
